name: In-LineLinc
description: The dual-band In-LineLinc dimmers and relays, which run the KeypadLinc code base with a single load. The relays ignore the ramp rate and on-level.

valueTables.name: rampRate
valueTables.description: How long each ramp rate takes to go from off to full on.

valueTables.name: onOff
valueTables.description: Off and on, for a load or LED a record switches.

operatingFlags.name: programmingLock
operatingFlags.label: Programming lock
operatingFlags.description: Linking and programming from the device itself are locked out.

operatingFlags.name: ledOnTransmit
operatingFlags.label: Blink LED when sending
operatingFlags.description: The status LED blinks when the device sends an Insteon message.

operatingFlags.name: resumeDim
operatingFlags.label: Resume dim
operatingFlags.description: Turning the load on at the device restores its last level instead of the on-level.

operatingFlags.name: ledOff
operatingFlags.label: LED off
operatingFlags.description: The status LEDs and button backlights are off.

verification.note: One source swaps 0x08 and 0x09 (backlight on and off); the values here are those other sources give. The Insteon Developer's Guide reads bit 4 of the 0x00 reply as LED on, but later sources read it as LED off, the state 0x08 sets.

operatingFlags.name: keyBeep
operatingFlags.label: Beep on button press
operatingFlags.description: The device beeps when a button is pressed.

verification.note: One source lists bit 5 of the 0x00 reply as load sense, set with 0x06 and 0x07; other sources make bit 5 the key beep on this code base.

operatingFlags.name: radioOff
operatingFlags.label: Turn off radio
operatingFlags.description: The device doesn't originate RF messages. It still repeats the RF messages it hears.

operatingFlags.name: powerLineOff
operatingFlags.label: Turn off powerline
operatingFlags.description: Insteon communication over the powerline is off. The device turns it back on whenever it powers up.

operatingFlags.name: applicationRetries
operatingFlags.label: Application retries
operatingFlags.description: The device retries application messages as many times as its ALL-Link database says, and reports cleanup errors.

operatingFlags.name: x10Off
operatingFlags.label: Turn off X10
operatingFlags.description: X10 sending and receiving are off.

operatingFlags.name: errorBlink
operatingFlags.label: Blink LED on errors
operatingFlags.description: The status LED blinks when a communication error occurs.

operatingFlags.name: cleanupReport
operatingFlags.label: Send cleanup reports
operatingFlags.description: The device sends a success report after the cleanup messages that follow a group command.

operatingFlags.name: checksumRequired
operatingFlags.label: Require checksums
operatingFlags.description: Extended Set and ALL-Link database write messages must carry a checksum in D14.

readings.name: databaseDelta
readings.label: ALL-Link database changes
readings.description: A count that goes up whenever the ALL-Link database changes.

readings.name: crcErrorCount
readings.label: CRC errors
readings.description: The number of messages received with a CRC error.

verification.note: The Insteon Developer's Guide gives query 0x02 as a signal-to-noise value; later sources count messages with CRC errors there.

flagCommands.name: smartHopsOn
flagCommands.description: Starts each message with the hop count of the last acknowledgment received (smart hops).

flagCommands.name: smartHopsOff
flagCommands.description: Starts each message with one hop.

flagCommands.name: yakityYakOff
flagCommands.description: Turns the Yakity Yak signaling option off.

flagCommands.name: yakityYakOn
flagCommands.description: Turns the Yakity Yak signaling option on.

flagCommands.name: modSyncFailureNoHop
flagCommands.description: When modulation sync fails, the device doesn't hop the message.

flagCommands.name: modSyncFailureOwnZeroCrossing
flagCommands.description: When modulation sync fails, the device uses its own zero crossing.

flagCommands.name: pushHopsToRadioOn
flagCommands.description: The device repeats every powerline hop over RF.

flagCommands.name: pushHopsToRadioOff
flagCommands.description: The device doesn't repeat every powerline hop over RF.

values.name: rampRate
values.label: Ramp rate
values.description: The ramp rate, from 0x01 (8 minutes) to 0x1F (0.1 second). 0x00 is 2 seconds.

verification.note: Earlier sources give ramp rate 0x00 as 9 minutes; the table uses the later reading, 2 seconds.

values.name: onLevel
values.label: On-level
values.description: The level the load turns on to, from 0x00 (off) to 0xFF (full).

values.name: ledBrightness
values.label: LED brightness
values.description: The brightness of the status LEDs, from 0x11 (dimmest) to 0x7F (brightest).

writes.name: ledBrightness
writes.description: Sets the brightness of the status LED.

standardCommands.name: lightOn
standardCommands.description: Turns the load on: a dimmer to the level in cmd2 at the saved ramp rate, an on/off model to full on.

parameter.name: onLevel
parameter.description: The level to go to, from 0x00 (off) to 0xFF (full).

standardCommands.name: lightOff
standardCommands.description: Turns the load off at the saved ramp rate.

standardCommands.name: readStatus
standardCommands.description: Reads the load's level. The acknowledgment's cmd1 carries the ALL-Link database delta.

reply.name: onLevel
reply.description: The load's level, from 0x00 (off) to 0xFF (full); an on/off model gives only 0x00 or 0xFF.

responder.name: onLevel
responder.label: On-level
responder.description: The level the group goes to when its controller's On arrives, 0x00 (off) to 0xFF (full). 0x00 makes the link off only.

verification.note: Read from the Insteon Developer's Guide, which gives Data 1 as the on-level and Data 2 as the ramp rate as examples, and from the KeypadLinc Line and LED Bulb Developer Notes. Inferred: seen on two i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48) linked to a Hub 2245, the device itself writes its responder record when it's linked remotely or with the SET button, and takes Data 1 from the load's state at that moment: the two plugs wrote 0x00 when the load was off and 0xFF when it was on. The On/Off Plug 2635-222 Owner's Manual says to make sure the module is on before linking it as a responder; the In-Line Dimmer Module (Dual-Band) 2475DA1 Owner's Manual says to set the load to the state the link should recall before linking it as a responder. The values given here are what to write when writing the record by hand.

responder.name: rampRate
responder.label: Ramp rate
responder.description: How fast the group goes to its on-level.

verification.note: Read from the Insteon Developer's Guide, which gives Data 1 as the on-level and Data 2 as the ramp rate as examples, and from the KeypadLinc Line and LED Bulb Developer Notes.

responder.name: onLevel
responder.label: On or off
responder.description: 0x00 turns the load off when the controller's On arrives, 0xFF on.

verification.note: Read from the On/Off Outlet and On/Off Module, Dual-Band Developer Notes, which give Data 1 as the on-level; no document describes this product's records. Inferred: seen on two i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48) linked to a Hub 2245, the device itself writes its responder record when it's linked remotely or with the SET button, and takes Data 1 from the load's state at that moment: the two plugs wrote 0x00 when the load was off and 0xFF when it was on. The On/Off Plug 2635-222 Owner's Manual says to make sure the module is on before linking it as a responder; the In-LineLinc On/Off 2475SDB Owner's Manual says to set the load to the state the link should recall before linking it as a responder. The values given here are what to write when writing the record by hand.
No document says that every nonzero level means on; the ranges are read from Light Status Request's level byte (cmd2), as the Insteon Developer's Guide describes it for on/off devices.

notes: Earlier sources give ramp rates 0x00 through 0x1F as 9 minutes down to 0.1 second; the later ones make 0x01 8 minutes and 0x00 2 seconds.
